specification.family_title: Connection recovery and unsafe pool reuse
specification.title: The backend of a failing transaction is terminated before its ROLLBACK; then the next unit of work runs on the same pool
steps: Unit 1: start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Checkpoint `unit1-after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). The runner terminates that backend and waits until it has gone. Then wait settle_ms.
Raise an application error inside the transaction. The framework attempts ROLLBACK on the closed connection, which fails.
Checkpoint `after-unit1`: report the same backend PID; the runner records that session's state.

Unit 2, the next unit of work on the same pool: start a transaction, write the marker `next`, checkpoint `unit2-after-write` (report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid()), and end normally. Give up after settings.bound_ms and report the unit as pending.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: Unrelated work never runs inside, or commits, a transaction whose rollback failed: that transaction is never committed, and the next unit of work runs in a transaction of its own.
After the failure, the next unit of work on the same pool completes within the bound (settings.bound_ms) and commits.

execution.description: The correct completion policy. NpgsqlDataSource with MaxPoolSize 1 and the driver's default reset on close. TX-03 only, plus the observation controls. The connection is returned to the pool when the unit finishes.

configuration.commit_outcome: CommitAsync after SELECT 1; rolled_back when the probe failed with 25P02; the command tag is not read

execution.form: The next unit receives the same connection when the policy kept it, or a new checkout when the policy disposed it. pooled uses NpgsqlDataSource with MaxPoolSize 1. It is not a framework pool.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: Inside unit 1, after its write, before the framework's ROLLBACK.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and unit 1's transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: An error from the framework's rollback; the pool holds a closed connection.

knowledge: The framework knows that its connection failed.

api_outcome.basis: the body threw and RollbackAsync threw. The connection was disposed. CommitAsync was not called.
api_outcome.contract: The correct npgsql-control policy uses NpgsqlConnection.BeginTransactionAsync, NpgsqlTransaction.CommitAsync, RollbackAsync, SaveAsync, RollbackAsync(name), and ReleaseAsync. Npgsql 10.0.3 CommitAsync sends COMMIT and waits for CommandComplete and ReadyForQuery. ExecuteInternalCommand does not read the command tag. TransactionStatus on the connector is internal and is Idle after both a committed transaction and a COMMIT that PostgreSQL answered with ROLLBACK. The public transaction API does not expose either fact. Before CommitAsync the policy runs SELECT 1 on the same connection. SQLSTATE 25P02 means the session is in a failed transaction block. If that probe fails with 25P02 and CommitAsync returns, the policy reports rolled_back and says it did not read the tag. If the probe succeeds and CommitAsync returns, the policy reports committed. A return from CommitAsync with no probe is not reported as a commit. If CommitAsync throws, the policy reports failed and disposes the connection. If RollbackAsync throws, it disposes the connection and does not call CommitAsync. A failed RollbackAsync(savepoint) is followed by RollbackAsync of the surrounding transaction. IsolationLevel is passed to BeginTransactionAsync.

error.message: 57P01: terminating connection due to administrator command

unit2.basis: SELECT 1 succeeded before CommitAsync, so the session was not in a failed transaction block, and CommitAsync returned. The command tag is not exposed. The policy does not treat a bare return, with no prior probe, as a commit.

evaluation.reason: TX-03.1 held: failed transaction: xid 8269 rolled back at report time (`after-unit1`); doomed visible: false; next unit's transaction: 8270; TX-03.2 held: next unit: completed, reported committed after 44 ms; its transaction: 8270 committed; next visible: true

preconditions.description: the write of marker "doomed" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit1-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "next" had reached PostgreSQL at `unit2-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the runner terminated the backend at `unit1-after-write`, and it had gone before the adapter resumed
the next unit of work was attempted
